attributes.aria-label: How to read the Apps hub

children: Pay, tip and connect with limits.
Choose the app by the job it has to do.
A Nostr app can be a client, signer, wallet connector, publishing desk, marketplace, media surface or developer tool. Start with the job, then read the profile, sources and trust boundary.

attributes.alt: Apps and products visual for the Nostr route

children: Start with the job, then read the trust and source trail.
Damus, Amethyst, Primal, Coracle, noStrudel and others are different windows into the same key-and-relay world.
Before a reader tests a web client, mobile app or wallet flow, they should know who is allowed to sign.
Zaps, NWC, Cashu wallets and Lightning tools turn app choice into a money-permission decision.
Habla, YakiHonne, Primal Reads, Highlighter and related tools show how Nostr becomes a publishing layer.
0xchat, Chachi, group tools and NIP-29 surfaces show the private and community side of Nostr apps.
Shopstr, Plebeian Market, Mostro and NIP-99 show the commercial edge of Nostr apps.
zap.stream, Wavlake, Olas, Nostr Nests and related tools turn Nostr into a creator surface.
nostr-tools, NDK, rust-nostr, nak and app frameworks explain how Nostr products are actually built.

children: Apps are grouped by what they do, from wallets and social clients to payment services, relays, communities, and developer tools. Well-known logos remain visible, but users can instantly see how each application fits into the ecosystem.
Wallet services and wallet apps that can sit behind a Nostr Wallet Connect app connection.

Payment products, checkout helpers, commerce-adjacent wallets and money-flow utilities.

Article, publishing, highlighting and long-read clients.
Chat, direct-message and encrypted conversation apps.
Live, event, video and creator-broadcast surfaces.
AI agents, assistants and machine-mediated tools that plug into Nostr or Lightning workflows.

Playful, game-like and challenge-based Nostr surfaces.
Music, audio, artist and listener apps.
Crowdfunding and campaign tools built around Bitcoin, Lightning or Nostr audiences.
Physical products and hardware-adjacent projects that bring payments or Nostr into the room.
Home-server and self-hosting systems that can host nodes, relays or wallet infrastructure.
Protocol pieces and authentication flows that other apps can build around.
Bots that move small Lightning payments through social spaces and chat rooms.
Exchange and swap surfaces that touch Lightning, Nostr identities or app payments.
Hosted node and wallet-service surfaces for users who do not want to run every piece locally.
Relay services, relay apps and infrastructure tools.
Useful ecosystem pieces, stores, directories, browsers and smaller tools that do not fit cleanly on another shelf.

children: Read the App route in the safest order.
The six route cards below are the reader path: start with a client, protect the key, add money carefully, choose the right publishing surface, verify sources and then build on standards.
Pick a client for the job first: mobile social, web exploration, publishing, chat or protocol learning.
Learn the signing boundary before trying every web client, mobile app, wallet tool or marketplace.
Use zaps and NWC through clear permissions, budgets, revocation paths and product-specific context.
Choose between notes, long-form, highlights, live video, photos, audio and creator tools by output.
Check official sites, repositories, app stores, NIPs and directory records before trusting product claims.
Use NIPs, SDKs, relays and test tools so a product does not become a private island.
